annotations.description: Playing Polluted Delta instead of Scalding Tarn means no red mana available this turn, missing the opportunity to cast Faithless Looting on turn 1. Faithless Looting is the ideal turn 1 play for this deck, fueling graveyard synergies with Emperor of Bones and Psychic Frog.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Polluted Delta, which can only fetch Island or Swamp (no red source).
annotations.betterLine: Play Scalding Tarn, fetch a Mountain (or a dual that produces red), then cast Faithless Looting turn 1 to dig and fill the graveyard.

annotations.description: Cracking Polluted Delta during their own postcombat main phase when they can't cast anything this turn anyway. There's no benefit to fetching now versus waiting until the opponent's end step, and cracking it now gives away information about their colors/deck unnecessarily.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Polluted Delta during own postcombat main phase on turn 1.
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn and crack Polluted Delta at the end of the opponent's turn to preserve information and maintain flexibility on which land to fetch.

annotations.description: Paid 2 life to have Watery Grave enter untapped on Turn 1 postcombat main phase with no instant-speed plays available for 1 mana. The hand contains Emperor of Bones (1B), Faithless Looting (R), Psychic Frog (UB), Raucous Theater, and Scalding Tarn — none of which can be meaningfully used with a single untapped UB source before Turn 2.
annotations.actionTaken: Paid 2 life to have Watery Grave enter untapped
annotations.betterLine: Let Watery Grave enter tapped, saving 2 life. It would be untapped by Turn 2 when the player can actually use multiple mana for their 2-drop spells.

annotations.description: Playing Raucous Theater (enters tapped) on turn 3 wastes the entire turn with no play, when Scalding Tarn could enter untapped and be cracked to enable casting Psychic Frog or Emperor of Bones this turn. With only 1 untapped land (Watery Grave), playing a tapped land means 0 additional mana this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Raucous Theater, which enters tapped, leaving only 1 mana available and no 2-mana play possible on turn 3.
annotations.betterLine: Play Scalding Tarn, crack it for a Swamp (or similar), then cast Psychic Frog (UB) or Emperor of Bones (1B) this turn. Save Raucous Theater for a turn where the tempo loss matters less.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones was chosen over Psychic Frog when both could be paired with Faithless Looting this turn. Psychic Frog is generally the stronger card - it synergizes beautifully with Faithless Looting (discard to grow), threatens card draw on combat damage, and can gain flying for evasion. Emperor of Bones lacks good reanimation targets currently.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Emperor of Bones
annotations.betterLine: Cast Psychic Frog ({U}{B}), then Faithless Looting ({R}) to draw 2 and discard 2 - discards can pump Frog and stock the graveyard for later use.

annotations.description: Casting Snapback (via alternate cost of exiling a blue card) to bounce Emperor of Bones, a 2/2 summoning sick creature that costs only {1}{B} to replay. This is a 2-for-0 card disadvantage (Snapback + exiled blue card) to delay a cheap creature by one turn. Emperor of Bones isn't an immediate lethal threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Snapback via alternate cost to bounce Emperor of Bones
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn and save Snapback and the blue card for a more impactful moment, such as bouncing a larger threat or protecting a combo turn. The 2/2 Emperor of Bones doesn't warrant spending two cards to delay by one turn.

annotations.description: Using Snapback's alternative cost (exiling a blue card from hand) to bounce a 2/2 Emperor of Bones that the opponent can simply replay next turn for 1B is a poor use of resources. This effectively costs two cards (Snapback + exiled blue card) to temporarily remove a small creature. With no lands in play and being in a desperate position, conserving resources for a more impactful use would be better.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Snapback (exiling a blue card) to bounce Emperor of Bones, a 2/2 that the opponent can cheaply replay next turn.
annotations.betterLine: Hold Snapback for a more threatening target or a situation where the tempo gain matters more. The opponent will simply replay Emperor of Bones next turn, making this a 2-for-0 card disadvantage for minimal tempo gain.

annotations.description: Using Snapback's alternative cost (exiling a blue card from hand) to bounce Emperor of Bones, a 2/2 that the opponent can easily recast next turn for {1}{B}. GPT52 Memoir is already severely resource-constrained with zero lands in play, and exiling a useful blue card for a temporary bounce of a small creature is questionable card economy. The opponent's lands are mostly tapped this turn anyway, limiting Emperor's immediate threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Snapback (exiling a blue card) to bounce Emperor of Bones
annotations.betterLine: Let the Lotus Bloom time counter resolve and save resources. Emperor of Bones is not immediately threatening since the opponent lacks mana to adapt it this turn, and the bounce is temporary. Preserving the blue card (likely Flare of Denial or a creature) could be more valuable later.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones exiled Snapback from opponent's graveyard instead of Goblin Charbelcher. The opponent's deck includes Tameshi, Reality Architect which can return artifact cards from graveyard to battlefield. Goblin Charbelcher is a major win condition/combo piece that could be recurred, while Snapback is a situational bounce spell with an alternate cost (exile a blue card) making the graveyard copy less critical.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Snapback from opponent's graveyard with Emperor of Bones trigger
annotations.betterLine: Exile Goblin Charbelcher to deny the opponent potential recursion of their combo piece via Tameshi or other graveyard-to-battlefield effects

annotations.description: Activated Adapt 2 on Emperor of Bones that already has +1/+1 counters. Adapt explicitly does nothing if the creature already has +1/+1 counters on it, so this wastes {1}{B} (2 mana) for zero effect. The Emperor is already 4/4 with two +1/+1 counters.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Adapt 2 on Emperor of Bones that already had +1/+1 counters, wasting 2 mana for no effect.
annotations.betterLine: Play Scalding Tarn (land drop), then cast Psychic Frog ({U}{B}) to develop another threat while still having mana available for Fatal Push or other plays. Alternatively, cast Faithless Looting to improve hand quality, or deploy the second Emperor of Bones.

annotations.description: Player was casting Disrupting Shoal to counter Psychic Frog (mana value 2) but timed out and failed to select a blue card to exile. This means Disrupting Shoal fails and Psychic Frog resolves. Psychic Frog is one of the most dangerous threats in Modern - it draws cards on combat damage, grows with discards, and can gain flying. Letting it resolve while also wasting the Disrupting Shoal is devastating.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out without selecting a card, causing Disrupting Shoal to fail and Psychic Frog to resolve.
annotations.betterLine: Exile Fallaji Archaeologist (mana value 2) to properly counter Psychic Frog with Disrupting Shoal, preserving Thundertrap Trainer for later card selection.

annotations.description: Fatal Push was cast with no enemy creatures on the battlefield, meaning the only valid target is MiMo's own Emperor of Bones (4/4). This destroys their own primary threat for absolutely no benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Fatal Push, presumably targeting their own Emperor of Bones 4/4
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority and proceed to combat, attacking with the 4/4 Emperor of Bones to pressure the opponent's 20 life total.

annotations.betterLine: Exile Psychic Frog from own graveyard, enabling reanimation via Emperor of Bones' adapt trigger to create a hasty Psychic Frog attacker

annotations.description: Failed to attack with a 4/4 Emperor of Bones into an empty board. The opponent has no creatures to block, so this is 4 free damage (20% of opponent's remaining life). The timeout caused the player to skip their attack entirely.
annotations.actionTaken: No response — skipped the attack step without declaring any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Emperor of Bones for 4 unblockable damage, bringing the opponent from 20 to 16 life.

annotations.description: Player timed out and took no action with Lotus Bloom as their only mana source and no lands in play. They had castable spells that would develop their board position against an opponent's 4/4 Emperor of Bones. Lotus Bloom is a one-shot resource that was wasted this turn. Fallaji Archaeologist would have provided a blocker, milled cards for future value, and enabled Flare of Denial as free countermagic.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed without casting anything, wasting the Lotus Bloom turn.
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice Lotus Bloom for {U}{U}{U}, cast Fallaji Archaeologist for {1}{U} (leaving {U} open), getting a 0/3 blocker, milling 3 cards, potentially finding a spell, and enabling Flare of Denial. Alternatively, cast Tameshi for {2}{U} to develop a bigger threat.

annotations.description: Casting Fallaji Archaeologist (0/3 for 2 mana) instead of Tameshi, Reality Architect (2/3 for 3 mana) when Lotus Bloom provides exactly 3 mana. Tameshi is a bigger body (relevant blocking Emperor of Bones 4/4), uses mana more efficiently (no waste), and could potentially recur Goblin Charbelcher from graveyard later. Both serve as blue creatures for Flare of Denial.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Fallaji Archaeologist for {1}{U}, leaving 1 mana unused from Lotus Bloom
annotations.betterLine: Cast Tameshi, Reality Architect for {2}{U}, using all 3 mana from Lotus Bloom efficiently, getting a bigger body and potential graveyard recursion

annotations.description: Playing Emperor of Bones before casting Faithless Looting is suboptimal sequencing. Faithless Looting costs only {R} and draws 2 cards while discarding 2, providing crucial information about what's available before committing to a play. If this was the activate option (Adapt), it does nothing since the Emperor already has +1/+1 counters. If casting a second copy, the legend rule would destroy the existing 4/4 to get a fresh 2/2, losing the +1/+1 counters.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Emperor of Bones (either activating Adapt on the 4/4 or casting a second copy) before seeing Faithless Looting draws.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Faithless Looting first for {R} to draw 2 cards and see more options, then decide whether to cast Emperor of Bones or take a different line based on what was drawn.

annotations.description: Failed to attack with a 4/4 Emperor of Bones into an empty board, missing 4 free damage against an opponent at 16 life. The opponent has no creatures to block. This was a timeout/no response rather than a deliberate choice.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not declare any attackers (timed out).
annotations.betterLine: Attack with the 4/4 Emperor of Bones for 4 unblocked damage, bringing the opponent from 16 to 12 life.

annotations.description: Disrupting Shoal was cast to counter Thoughtseize (MV 1), but with no lands in play and no blue card with MV 1 in hand, the only possible X value is 0. Disrupting Shoal with X=0 cannot counter a spell with MV 1, so this wastes the Disrupting Shoal for nothing while Thoughtseize still resolves.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Disrupting Shoal (which will have X=0) attempting to counter Thoughtseize (MV 1)
annotations.betterLine: Let Thoughtseize resolve. Losing a card to Thoughtseize is bad but at least you keep Disrupting Shoal for a future spell that might have MV 0, or save it for when you have mana to hard-cast it with appropriate X value.

annotations.description: Took Flare of Denial with Thoughtseize instead of the opponent's Goblin Charbelcher or a Whir of Invention. MiMo is the aggressor with 8 power on board vs opponent at 12 life, meaning the primary concern is the opponent comboing off with Charbelcher before being killed. Flare of Denial is less threatening since the opponent has no blue creatures to sacrifice for its alternate cost, and MiMo has almost nothing worth countering in hand (just Faithless Looting).
annotations.actionTaken: Took Flare of Denial from opponent's hand
annotations.betterLine: Take Goblin Charbelcher to prevent the combo kill, forcing the opponent to use Whir of Invention (requiring 7+ mana) to find another copy from the library, buying crucial time to attack for lethal.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones can only reanimate creature cards exiled with it. Lotus Bloom is an artifact and cannot be reanimated. Fallaji Archaeologist is a creature in the opponent's graveyard that could be reanimated when Emperor adapts, providing card advantage (mill 3 + potential card selection).
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Lotus Bloom with Emperor of Bones' combat trigger
annotations.betterLine: Exile Fallaji Archaeologist instead, giving this Emperor of Bones a creature reanimation target when it adapts for {1}{B}

annotations.description: The opponent is at 12 life with no creatures on the battlefield. MiMo has two 4/4 Emperor of Bones, one 2/2 Emperor of Bones, and a 1/2 Psychic Frog. Without pumping, total attack damage is 4+4+2+1=11, one short of lethal. Discarding Faithless Looting to Psychic Frog would make it 2/3, bringing total damage to exactly 12 — lethal. The player timed out and failed to activate the ability.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) — did not activate Psychic Frog's discard ability.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Faithless Looting to Psychic Frog to pump it to 2/3, then attack with all creatures for exactly 12 damage (lethal).

annotations.description: Failed to declare any attackers against an opponent at 12 life with NO blockers on the battlefield. Had two 4/4 Emperor of Bones, one 2/2 Emperor of Bones, and a 1/2 Psychic Frog available to attack for 11 total damage, putting the opponent to 1 life. The Psychic Frog would also draw a card on combat damage. This was a timeout/no response that wasted a critical attack opportunity.
annotations.actionTaken: No attackers declared (timeout/no response)
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures (11 damage total) to put the opponent to 1 life, with Psychic Frog drawing a card on damage. This likely wins the game next turn.
